title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Microsoft Azure
providers.scope_notes: Covers Microsoft Azure (Azure Storage, Azure Resource Manager, Microsoft Entra Workload ID, Azure DevOps Services). Azure Storage and ARM controls are per subscription/account; Conditional Access for workload identities needs Workload Identities Premium; Azure DevOps PAT policies need an Entra-backed organization. Entra delegated/app-only OAuth for Graph and managed identities are covered by the separate microsoft platform.

controls.name: Conditional Access for workload identities
controls.what: Blocks token requests by single-tenant service principals from outside named locations or when risky.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Conditional Access > Workload identities

controls.name: App management policy (passwordAddition, passwordLifetime, asymmetricKeyLifetime)
controls.what: Blocks new password secrets or caps secret/certificate lifetimes for new or updated apps.

controls.name: Remove credential / disable service principal
controls.what: Deleting the secret, certificate or federated credential stops new token requests; disabling the SP is a CAE revocation event for Microsoft Graph only.
controls.setting: App registrations > Certificates & secrets; Enterprise applications > Properties

controls.name: Azure RBAC role assignment scope
controls.what: Service principal ARM access is limited to its assigned roles and scopes.

controls.name: Block password addition (passwordAddition restriction)
controls.what: Blocks adding new client secrets to applications and service principals; certificates are not blocked by this restriction.
controls.setting: Entra ID > Enterprise apps > Application policies > Block password addition (or tenantAppManagementPolicy via Microsoft Graph)

controls.name: Users can register applications
controls.what: Set to No so only admins and Application Developer role holders can create app registrations (and so add secrets, certificates or federated credentials to new apps).
controls.setting: Entra ID > Users > User settings > Users can register applications

no_control.what: CAE for workload identities does not cover Azure Resource Manager; ARM tokens survive SP disable until expiry.
App management policies do not affect existing credentials or token issuance for existing apps.

controls_unknown: Whether Azure Activity Log records the service principal identity for ARM read calls made with azure-3/azure-4 tokens (Activity log typically skips reads).

auth_paths.name: Service principal client secrets and certificates (used against Azure Resource Manager)

authentication.summary: App registration secret or certificate used in the client credentials flow to get an Entra access token for Azure Resource Manager; access is set by Azure RBAC role assignments.

federation.details: Not a user sign-in. Conditional Access for workload identities can block by location or risk, but only at token request and only for single-tenant SPs, and needs Workload Identities Premium.

ip_restriction.boundary: Location-based Conditional Access for workload identities blocks token requests from outside allowed ranges. Already-issued ARM tokens are not re-checked (CAE for workload identities is Microsoft Graph only).

lifetime.summary: Secret up to 24 months; access tokens 60-90 min

renewal.summary: Secret or certificate is reused to request new access tokens until it expires or is removed.

administration.summary: App management policies can block new password secrets or cap secret/certificate lifetimes; they do not affect existing apps. Credentials are removed in the app registration; the SP can be disabled.
administration.conditions: Tenant default policy is disabled by default.

sso.details: Conditional Access for workload identities applies to single-tenant service principals only and needs Workload Identities Premium; multitenant apps are not covered.

offboard.details: Client secrets and certificates belong to the application/service principal, not a user.

inventory.details: Each application object exposes its passwordCredentials and keyCredentials collections through Microsoft Graph (GET /applications).

sso.ui: Entra admin center > Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy > Users or workload identities > What does this policy apply to? = Workload identities > select service principals

expiry.ui: Entra admin center > Entra ID > Enterprise apps > Application policies > Restrict max password lifetime / Restrict max certificate lifetime

usage.ui: Entra admin center > Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs > Service principal sign-ins; filter by application ID

reads.ui: Storage account (or subscription) > Activity log; filter Operation to listkeys action and caller = the app ID

kill.ui: Disable the service principal (accountEnabled = false) and delete the secret/certificate on the app registration

log_sources.name: Microsoft Entra service principal sign-in logs
log_sources.notes: Token requests with secret/certificate; 7 days (Free) or 30 days (P1/P2).

log_sources.name: Azure Activity Log
log_sources.notes: Control-plane writes/actions (e.g. listKeys, regenerateKey); 90 days free; reads typically not captured.

credential_id_fields.notes: Credential used is a secret or certificate.

lifecycle_events.event: Update application - Certificates and secrets management

anomaly_cues: New secret added to a privileged app

containment.steps: Remove the secret/certificate, disable the SP, and remove role assignments.
containment.notes: ARM access tokens remain valid until expiry (60-90 min); CAE for workload identities covers Microsoft Graph only.

calls.log_notes: Activity log typically does not capture reads; token request is in SP sign-in logs.

unknown: Exact Activity Log behavior for listKeys not quoted on fetched page.
